_doc: Sector adaptation registry. Keyed by the MCP `industry` field from search_tickerid (the MCP's industry level, e.g. 'Health Care'), NOT `insync_subindustry` ('Biotech and Pharma'). financial_rows overrides the default income-statement template. kpi_code_whitelist and kpi_keywords are ADVISORY: they guide the model's KPI selection and are not read by compute_tearsheet.py. suppress_valuation removes analytically inappropriate multiples. A profile is only required where the default template (Revenue/Gross Profit/EBIT/EBITDA/EPS) does not fit the P&L; most operating sectors need no entry and fall back cleanly.

Financial Services._note: Brokers, exchanges, asset managers, specialty finance. No gross profit, EBIT or EBITDA is reported; EV is not meaningful when debt is an operating input.

Insurance._note: Underwriters. Revenue is premiums plus investment income; no gross profit, EBIT or EBITDA. Book value and combined ratio carry the analysis.

Real Estate._note: REITs and property owners. No gross profit line. v7.2.16: the P&L rows are FFO/AFFO based, not EBIT/EPS based, and P/E and PEG are SUPPRESSED rather than merely discouraged in prose - a REIT's P/E is depreciation noise and the old note asking the model to caveat it depended on the model remembering. EV/EBITDA is retained: it is standard for property. FFO and AFFO per share are tagged top_kpi by the MCP, so the KPI block already reaches them. P/FFO is not a get_valuation metric, so it is COMPUTED from the price and the FY1 consensus FFO/share via computed_valuation, and leads the strip.

Industrial Products._note: Industrial and aerospace manufacturers. v7.2.17: IS_P_267 (Cost & Expenses) added to the whitelist - the MCP tags it top_kpi for pre-commercial names such as an early-stage aircraft maker, where cost growth IS the story because revenue has barely started, and the v7.2.16 thin-profile warning flagged its absence on a real run.

Oil and Gas._note: E&P and integrated oil. v7.2.17: the profile had kpi_keywords only, so the default template applied and asked for Gross Profit / EBIT / EBITDA. A large E&P issuer returns NOTHING for IS_P_113 (EBITDA) - the E&P earnings line is EBITDAX, IS_P_172, which the MCP tags top_kpi|industry_kpi. That is why every E&P sheet carried 'THIN FINANCIALS: only 4 of the prescribed rows populated'. Verified on a large E&P issuer: revenue, EBITDAX, total production expense and adjusted EPS all populate. No gross profit line.

_lower_is_better_note: v7.2.0. lower_is_better_rows lists financial_rows LTCODEs that are COSTS, so a rise in them is coloured as bad news rather than good. lower_is_better_codes lists KPI LTCODEs whose polarity is inverted (efficiency ratio, combined ratio, medical loss ratio, churn, any cost line): a LOWER value beats the estimate. Without them, polarity would have to be re-supplied by the model in raw_data.json on every run with nothing checking it — the Banking, Financial Services and Insurance kpi_keywords steer straight at these metrics. A code listed here is treated as inverted even when raw_data.json omits the flag.

Utilities._note: Regulated electric, gas and water utilities. v7.2.17: NEW. Deliberately does NOT suppress P/E or PEG - unlike a REIT, a utility's earnings are real regulated earnings and P/E is the metric the sector trades on. What the default template misses is INTEREST EXPENSE, which for a rate-base-funded balance sheet is a first-order line. Verified on a large US electric utility (2Q26): every row in this template populated, Interest Expenses included. Note the top_kpi set for a utility is company-specific segment revenue (a named subsidiary's revenue, and so on), so there is no useful kpi_code_whitelist here - keywords are the right lever.

Industrial Services._note: Transportation, logistics and shipping. v7.2.17: NEW, and deliberately KEYWORDS ONLY. One carrier's entire top_kpi set is company-specific segment and volume lines (route volumes, segment EBIT, and so on), so a kpi_code_whitelist would be wrong here - it would encode one company's segments as the sector's metrics. The default income-statement template fits the P&L; what the model needs is steering toward volumes and rates, which is what these keywords do.

Real Estate (non-REIT)._note: v8.1.0. Real estate services firms and developers (measured 2026-10-13) report no FFO, AFFO or NOI, so the REIT rows came back empty and P/E was suppressed on a company valued on P/E. Reached only through _by_subindustry. No financial_rows: the default adjusted-first template applies (a large services firm fills all six rows). P/E is not suppressed.
